questions.stem:
(a) State four functions of an office. [4 marks]
(b) Distinguish between a private secretary and a company secretary. [4 marks]
(c) State four advantages of the open office layout. [4 marks]
(d) State four personal attributes expected of office staff. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) any four: receiving information; recording information; processing information; giving information; storing information; safeguarding assets (1 mark each)
2 marks: (b) a private secretary works for an individual executive, handling correspondence, appointments and confidential matters
2 marks: (b) a company secretary is a statutory officer responsible for legal compliance, statutory books, meetings and returns of a company
4 marks: (c) any four: easy supervision; saves space and cost; easy communication; equipment can be shared; flexible rearrangement; uniform conditions (1 mark each)
4 marks: (d) any four: neat appearance; punctuality; honesty; politeness; good personal hygiene; loyalty; confidentiality (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: The office receives, records, processes, gives and stores information and safeguards assets. A private secretary serves an executive; a company secretary is a statutory officer. Open offices aid supervision, save cost and ease communication. Staff should be neat, punctual, honest, polite and discreet.

questions.stem:
Mr Femi Ojo is paid a basic salary of ₦180,000 a month. He receives a housing allowance of ₦40,000 and a transport allowance of ₦25,000. Deductions are PAYE tax ₦21,000, pension contribution ₦16,000 and union dues ₦2,000.
(a) Calculate his: (i) gross pay; (ii) total deductions; (iii) net pay. [6 marks]
(b) Explain the following methods of paying workers: (i) piece rate; (ii) time rate; (iii) commission. [6 marks]
(c) Explain PAYE. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) gross pay = 180,000 + 40,000 + 25,000 = ₦245,000
2 marks: (a)(ii) deductions = 21,000 + 16,000 + 2,000 = ₦39,000
2 marks: (a)(iii) net pay = 245,000 - 39,000 = ₦206,000
2 marks: (b)(i) piece rate: payment according to the number of units produced
2 marks: (b)(ii) time rate: payment according to the time worked, e.g. per hour or day
2 marks: (b)(iii) commission: payment as a percentage of the value of sales made
4 marks: (c) Pay As You Earn: income tax deducted by the employer from employees' pay each pay period and remitted to the tax authority
questions.explanation: Gross pay ₦245,000; deductions ₦39,000; net pay ₦206,000. Piece rate pays per unit, time rate per hour or day, commission as a percentage of sales. PAYE is income tax deducted at source by the employer and paid to the tax authority.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three parties to a cheque. [3 marks]
(b) State four features of a valid cheque. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the following crossings: (i) general crossing; (ii) special crossing; (iii) 'Account Payee Only'. [6 marks]
(d) State three functions of a commercial bank. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) drawer; drawee (bank); payee (1 mark each)
4 marks: (b) any four: date; name of payee; amount in words and figures agreeing; signature of drawer; written on the bank's cheque leaf; not stale (1 mark each)
2 marks: (c)(i) general crossing: two parallel lines across the face, with or without "& Co."; the cheque must be paid into a bank account
2 marks: (c)(ii) special crossing: the name of a particular bank written between the lines; payable only through that bank
2 marks: (c)(iii) Account Payee Only: the proceeds must be paid into the account of the named payee
3 marks: (d) any three: accepting deposits; granting loans and overdrafts; providing means of payment (cheques, cards, transfers); safe keeping of valuables; foreign exchange services (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Parties: drawer, drawee and payee. A valid cheque is dated, signed, names the payee and has matching words and figures. General crossing requires payment into a bank; special crossing names the bank; Account Payee Only restricts payment to the payee's account. Commercial banks accept deposits, lend and provide payment services.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between vertical, horizontal and diagonal communication. [6 marks]
(b) Explain four barriers to effective communication in an office. [8 marks]
(c) What is a quorum? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) vertical: between superiors and subordinates, upward or downward
2 marks: (a) horizontal: between people at the same level, e.g. heads of departments
2 marks: (a) diagonal: between people in different departments and at different levels
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: physical barriers (noise, distance); language/jargon; psychological barriers (emotions, prejudice); organisational barriers (long chain of command); socio-cultural differences; poor choice of medium
2 marks: (c) the minimum number of members that must be present for a meeting to be valid
questions.explanation: Vertical communication goes up or down the hierarchy; horizontal between equals; diagonal across departments and levels. Barriers include noise, jargon, emotions, long chains of command and cultural differences. A quorum is the minimum attendance for a valid meeting.

questions.stem:
(a) State four features of a good filing system. [4 marks]
(b) Distinguish between centralised and departmental filing, stating one advantage of each. [6 marks]
(c) State three advantages and three disadvantages of electronic filing. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) any four: simple to operate; economical; secure/confidential; allows quick retrieval; flexible for expansion; compact; suitable for the organisation (1 mark each)
3 marks: (b) centralised: all files kept in one place under specialist staff; advantage: uniform system/better supervision/saves equipment
3 marks: (b) departmental: each department keeps its own files; advantage: files are near users/quicker access/confidential within department
3 marks: (c) advantages, any three: saves space; fast retrieval; easy to copy and share; easy backup (1 mark each)
3 marks: (c) disadvantages, any three: depends on electricity; risk of viruses/hacking; costly equipment; data loss if no backup; needs trained staff (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: A good filing system is simple, cheap, secure, compact, flexible and quick. Centralised filing keeps all records in one place with uniform control; departmental filing keeps files near users. Electronic filing saves space and is fast but depends on power and is vulnerable to viruses.

questions.stem:
Read the case study and answer the questions.
Aisha Bello has just completed her secondary education with a credit in Clerical Office Duties. She sees an advertisement in a newspaper for the post of Office Assistant at Crescent Ventures Ltd, Kaduna. The advertisement asks applicants to apply in their own handwriting with a CV and two references, within two weeks. Aisha writes a short letter on a page torn from an exercise book, does not state the position she is applying for, and attaches no CV. She is not invited for interview.
(a) State four items of information that should appear in a job advertisement. [4 marks]
(b) Identify three mistakes Aisha made in her application. [6 marks]
(c) List four sections that should be included in Aisha's curriculum vitae. [4 marks]
(d) State four things Aisha should do to prepare for an interview if she is invited in future. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) any four: job title; duties; qualifications/experience required; salary or benefits; method of application; closing date; name and address of employer (1 mark each)
6 marks: (b) any three, 2 marks each: used torn exercise-book paper instead of clean paper; did not state the position applied for; did not attach a CV; did not include references; letter too brief
4 marks: (c) any four: personal details; educational background; qualifications obtained; work experience; skills/hobbies; referees (1 mark each)
8 marks: (d) any four, 2 marks each: research the company; dress neatly and appropriately; arrive early; prepare answers to common questions; take original certificates and documents; be confident and polite
questions.explanation: An advert should give the job title, duties, requirements, salary, method of application and closing date. Aisha used poor paper, omitted the post, the CV and references. A CV includes personal details, education, qualifications, experience, skills and referees. For interviews she should research the firm, dress well, arrive early and take her documents.
